name: Member stop payment request
description: Record a stop payment against a member's share draft in the MeridianCore servicing console and return the host reference number from the confirmation screen. The committing control is human-only under the default safety profile, so an unattended replay pauses for an operator before the request is recorded.

inputs.name: member_id
inputs.description: The member number the stop payment is recorded against.

inputs.name: check_number

business_outcomes.name: member_not_found

params.text: No member matching that number was found.

when.description: the screen shows 'No member matching that number was found.'

business_outcomes.message: The member number searched does not exist in the system. The console displays "No member matching that number was found." along with "Searched member number: {number}". This is a legitimate business answer, not a system fault — the caller should be told the member could not be located.

business_outcomes.name: invalid_check_number_format

when.description: the screen shows 'Check number must be numeric.'

business_outcomes.message: When a non-numeric value is entered in the Check Number field on the Stop Payment Request form and the form is submitted, the console rejects the submission and displays the inline validation message "Check number must be numeric." This is a caller data-entry mistake, not a system fault — the form remains open for correction.

recovery_rules.description: After signing on and before the first Member Servicing search, a "System Notice" interstitial appears announcing a scheduled maintenance window. It is shown once per sign-on and is cleared by clicking the "Acknowledge and Continue" button, after which the requested Member Servicing screen loads normally.

recovery_rules.name: session_timeout

params.text: Session Ended Your session has expired. Sign on again to continue.

when.description: the screen shows 'Session Ended Your session has expired. Sign on again to con'

recovery_rules.description: If the operator session has expired, navigating to any function (e.g. Member Servicing) shows a "Session Ended" dialog stating "Your session has expired." and "Sign on again to continue." with a "Return to Sign On" button. Unlike a simple interstitial, clearing this does not resume the interrupted step in place — it returns to the Operator Sign On screen, so a replay that encounters this must restart the entire flow from sign-on (operator id + passcode) rather than retrying the step that noticed the timeout. Restarts the flow from the entry point, because dismissing this screen alone leaves the session unauthenticated.

failure_rules.name: host_transaction_failure

params.text: SYSTEM ERROR MC-5001 The host transaction could not be completed. Contact the service desk with this reference.

when.description: the screen shows 'SYSTEM ERROR MC-5001 The host transaction could not be compl'

failure_rules.message: When submitting the Stop Payment request while the host is in a fault state, the console displays an "Application Error" dialog with the title "SYSTEM ERROR MC-5001" and body text "The host transaction could not be completed. Contact the service desk with this reference." This is a genuine application/host fault, not a business outcome — the run must stop and be treated as failed/incomplete rather than as a successfully recorded stop payment, since no Reference Number or Request Status confirmation is produced.

provenance.goal: Sign on to the MeridianCore servicing console and open Member Servicing. Look up the member whose number is given by the member_id input. From that member's record, open Stop Payment. On the request form, leave the Draft Account at the account already selected, enter the Check Number, the Check Amount and the Requested By name from the inputs of the same names, and choose the reason "Check lost or stolen". Then place the stop payment. The flow is only complete when the confirmation screen is on screen: read the Reference Number and the Request Status from it.
provenance.notes: dropped the step that dismissed the interstitial ('Dismiss the system notice to proceed to Member Servicing'); it is covered by a recovery rule, which fires whenever the screen appears
